• Setting a high bar for engineering excellence through strong technical judgment and organizational leadership

• Building and sustaining high-performance teams with a focus on accountability, ownership, and continuous improvement

• Operating with ownership and delivering measurable outcomes in fast-paced, complex environments

Outside of the office, we invest in your well-being and learning & development with stipends and reimbursement programs.

title: Global Sanctions Manager
description:
ABOUT AIRWALLEX

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,300 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles https://www.airwallex.com/en-us/operating-principles to see it in full.

 

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Regulatory & Compliance Team at Airwallex is a global, collaborative function comprised of experts in their respective subject matters. We provide trusted guidance across the business, strengthen our regulatory and compliance framework, and promote a culture of compliance, sound risk management, and ethical conduct across Airwallex.

The Financial Crime Compliance (FCC) team is a strategically important second-line function, responsible for Airwallex’s Global AML/CTF and Sanctions frameworks. As Airwallex expands into new markets and deepens its engagement with regulators and financial institution partners, the FCC team helps manage complex financial crime risks across a growing global business.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

As a Global Sanctions Manager, you will have the unique opportunity to drive high-impact global initiatives to ensure Airwallex successfully navigates the world of economic sanctions as the business and compliance function continue to scale. As a truly global company building cross-border financial infrastructure, sanctions compliance is a critical component to our long term success. Come join a team where you will see the immediate impact of your work.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

- Act as a Sanctions Subject Matter Expert (SME) and serve as the ultimate second-line escalation point for highly complex, ambiguous sanctions matches, special investigations, and potential block-and-reject reporting.

- Own and maintain Global Sanctions procedures and provide effective second-line oversight of sanctions controls implemented by first-line teams.

- Compile management information and develop comprehensive dashboards to track the health and effectiveness of the sanctions compliance program.

- Assist in the maintenance, tuning, and optimization of sanctions screening technologies, list management systems, and case management platforms to ensure alerts are accurate and efficient.

- Partner with Risk Product teams to design, evaluate, and implement product-specific sanctions controls that align with global regulatory requirements.

- Monitor global sanctions and export-control developments, translating complex regulatory changes into practical, scalable control enhancements and delivering targeted training across the business.

- Deliver tailored sanctions training and written regulatory updates to Global Airwallex teams, covering alert adjudication, escalation procedures, and critical policy changes.

- Lead responses to banking partners and other external stakeholders on sanctions-related inquiries and due diligence reviews.

WHO YOU ARE

We're looking for people who meet the minimum requirements for this role. The preferred qualifications are great to have, but are not mandatory.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

- 7+ years of relevant experience, preferably at a fintech, payments company, or large financial institution specializing in sanctions.

- Demonstrated understanding of US sanctions and industry best

title: Business Analyst (Year in Industry)
description:
The Global Business Development & Digital Strategy team, split evenly between New York and London, focuses on executing and renewing revenue-generating commercial deals monetizing Sony Music’s vast catalogue with a broad range of companies globally, from major streaming partners such as Spotify, Amazon, Apple, YouTube and TikTok to the next generation of music and technology start-ups. You will join an international team of data-savvy negotiators and business analysts, who operate on the front lines with strong work ethic and genuine team spirit. If you're a penultimate-year undergraduate looking for a placement year, this is an opportunity to spend 12 months at the centre of the global music industry's digital transformation.
 
During your Year in Industry as Business Analyst, you will be trained and exposed to digital distribution deal structures and strategies. You will gain an understanding of how music copyrights are licensed, of the general structure of our industry, and of how commercial agreements with global and multi-territory digital partners are negotiated and executed. You will grow your ability to summarise complex thoughts, crystallise situations and potential options, isolate action points and communicate them effectively in writing to stakeholders. What makes this role unusual is the level of exposure. You'll have the opportunity to work directly with analysts, dealmakers and senior leaders in London and New York, gaining insight into commercial decision-making that most students only encounter years into their careers.
 
You will prepare and maintain benchmarking analysis tools and contribute to ad hoc projects including researching markets and business opportunities, documenting and comparing commercial agreements, building revenue forecasts and conducting in depth business analysis while working closely with negotiators and senior business analysts. You will establish yourself as a point of contact for queries relating to these areas by forging strong relationships across the business and with external contacts.

title: Classified Platform Engineer
tags: Corporate Technology : Classified Systems : Classified Infrastructure
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Anduril is seeking a Classified Platform Engineer to serve as the technical lead for our classified software team. You will design and build the platform services and user-facing applications that make multi-level classified computing possible: a virtual desktop and application broker, a policy-enforcing storage gateway, and the administrative interfaces for our access control platform. You will own them end to end, from architecture through the DevSecOps pipeline that delivers them into accredited, fully air-gapped environments, working alongside Cybersecurity, Systems Engineering, and Infrastructure Engineering.

This is a hands-on role with real technical authority. You will be the first dedicated software engineer on this team, which means you set the architecture, choose the patterns, and establish the engineering standards the rest of the team builds to. As the team grows you will lead it technically, and there is a clear path into formal technical leadership of the software function for someone who wants it.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Act as technical lead for the classified software and platform team: own the architecture of the application portfolio, set the standards the team builds to, and make the tradeoff calls.

• Design and build production web applications in React and Go that operate fully air-gapped inside accredited classified environments.

• Develop and work with S3 storage APIs and policies.

• Build the administrative and operator interfaces for our access control platform, and design the relational and distributed datastores behind authorization decisions, audit records, and application state.

• Own the DevSecOps path to production: containerize and deploy to Kubernetes through GitOps CI/CD pipelines that scan, sign, and produce the evidence our accreditations require.

• Decompose multi-quarter programs into well-scoped work other engineers can deliver independently, and grow the engineers who join the team through design review, code review, and pairing.

• Partner with Cybersecurity, Program Management, and business line stakeholders to capture requirements and translate them into a technical plan delivered on time and on budget.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Professional experience building and shipping production web applications with React, or a comparable modern front-end framework, and TypeScript, including interfaces for complex domains where operator workflow matters.

• Professional experience developing backend services in Go.

• Experience designing and working with relational databases such as PostgreSQL or CockroachDB, including schema design, migrations, and query performance.

• Experience with containerization and container orchestration (Podman or Docker, and Kubernetes), and with GitOps and Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipelines in an Agile development process.

• Knowledge and experience with Linux Operating Systems (OS) such as Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), Rocky Linux, or Ubuntu.

• Experience leading technical work: owning a system's architecture, reviewing the designs and code of others, setting direction for a small team, and communicating clearly in design documents, tradeoff analyses, and decision records a peer can pick up and act

We improve healthcare workflows and help patients start and stay on therapy with end-to-end solutions that enhance prescription access, affordability, and adherence. Our solutions help 100 million patients a year and are used by more than 420,000 prescribers, 71,000 pharmacies, 270 EHRs and health information systems, and over 2,000 hospitals in the U.S. This is a great opportunity to be a part of a successful Healthcare IT company experiencing significant growth. Here you'll get to work with some of the smartest and most interesting people around; solving unique and complex challenges in healthcare on a scale matched by a few companies. If you get excited about stretching yourself in new ways, developing yourself to your fullest potential, care about working with smart colleagues; we want to talk to you!
Position Overview
DrFirst is building an agentic ecosystem at scale. In the last 90 days we have shipped production AI systems across HR, Finance, Legal, and Marketing, automating hundreds of hours of manual work monthly and delivering measurable business impact.
This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You architect and build production AI automation systems from discovery to deployment. You work directly with department leaders to map workflows and ship tools that augment their work.
The split is 80% individual-contributor engineering and 20% servant leadership and mentorship. You build. You own technical architecture decisions. As the team scales from 2 to 5-6 engineers over 18 months, you mentor through code review and pairing. You also teach non-technical department leaders how to use AI tools, translate technical concepts for executives, and run discovery sessions that extract workflows from stakeholders. Building stays your primary focus.
Who Will Love This Job

• You are a senior IC who loves shipping code daily. You have been a Staff or Principal Engineer or led small teams, but you miss hands-on building.

• You can architect multi-agent systems and run discovery sessions with department VPs to map their workflows.

• You can debug OAuth2 flows through enterprise proxies and explain security requirements to non-technical stakeholders.

• You are a servant leader. You remove blockers for others, teach through pairing rather than directives, and make stakeholders successful.

• You organize chaos: 15 stakeholders, 6 systems, 3 sprints in flight. You ask “How can I help?” before “Here is what you should do.”

What you will work on
Build Production AI Automation (80%)
You own the technical implementation of department sprints. Example: an HR sprint delivered resume screening (40-candidate PDF extraction with table-of-contents parsing and fuzzy name matching), OKR coaching (Leapsome API integration with performance rating analytics), performance ratings (calibration detection across 328 employees), and milestone email automation in 4 weeks.

•
Architecture and Implementation: Design and build Python/FastAPI backends connecting to enterprise APIs (HRIS, ERP, CRM, finance systems, project management).

•
Frontend Development: Build Next.js/React frontends with Okta SSO, role-based access control, and audit trails.

•
Multi-Agent Systems: Design agent coordination systems, skill discovery hubs, agent registries, and workflow orchestration.

•
Enterprise Integration: Navigate Zscaler proxies, VPNs, SSL certificates, Kubernetes pod networking, DynamoDB, and AWS Bedrock.

•
Testing and Quality: Write Playwright end-to-end tests before production deploy and maintain a 1000+ test suite with visual regression baselines.

•
Deployment: Ship via GitLab CI/CD to AWS EKS (Kubernetes, ArgoCD, Helm, Secrets Manager) and diagnose pod restarts and liveness probe issues.

•
Async and Performance: Debug event loop blocking, convert synchronous I/O to async, and optimize CPU-bound operations.

title: Firmware Automation Engineer
description:
Imagine a future where everyone has instant, low-cost access to intelligence. We’re building a fully featured European AI cloud - with everything one needs to train, experiment with, and deploy AI models. In addition, our GPUs run on 100% renewable energy.
We’re ambitious, curious, and gutsy doers. We practice a low hierarchy across the company and high morale in our teams. We’ve already achieved a lot, yet we’re only getting started. Now it’s your chance to join the ride. We offer more than just the job - we offer a career-defining opportunity to be part of building something big!
Join Verda while it’s still being built - not once it’s finished.
About the role
Instead of traditional systems engineering, your focus will be entirely on the silicon and low-level software layers. You will design, build, and maintain the automation frameworks that keep our entire fleet up to date-covering everything from motherboards and Baseboard Management Controllers (BMCs) to high-performance InfiniBand fabrics and GPU clusters. In our "move fast" culture, your job is to build the safety nets (health checks, canary deploys, and automated rollbacks) that allow us to update hardware rapidly without taking down the cloud.
Your Responsibilities

• Fleet-Wide Firmware Orchestration: Design and execute automated, zero-touch firmware update pipelines across our global fleet of servers, switches, and accelerators.

• Heterogeneous Hardware Management: Own the firmware lifecycle for multiple hardware profiles, including Systemboards (BIOS/UEFI), BMCs, InfiniBand HCAs, Network Switches, and high-performance GPUs.

• Redfish & API Automation: Leverage Redfish and IPMI APIs to programmatically discover, configure, inventory, and update bare-metal assets at scale.

• Build Blast-Radius Protections: Architect robust telemetry pipelines to assess hardware health post-flash, and build automated rollback mechanisms to instantly recover from faulty vendor payloads.

• Tooling & Infrastructure as Code: Integrate firmware management pipelines cleanly into our existing configuration management ecosystems (SaltStack/Ansible) and provisioning workflows.

• Vendor & Engineering Liaison: Deep-dive into hardware errata and bug reports, collaborating closely with hardware vendors and internal platform teams to patch critical CVEs and performance regressions.

Your key competencies

• Automation at Scale: Proven experience managing and updating firmware across thousands of nodes simultaneously. You don't do "one-off" flashes; you write code to update clusters.

• Deep Redfish Expertise: Mastery of the DMTF Redfish specification for server management, out-of-band communication, and telemetry collection.

• Hardware Polyglot: Strong understanding of the architectural differences in managing firmware across systemboards, network stacks (InfiniBand/Ethernet), and GPU architectures.

• Failure Domain Expertise: A paranoid mindset regarding hardware health. You know how to verify if a device is truly healthy post-boot and how to safely execute an unattended rollback if it isn't.

• Scripting & Infrastructure Code: Proficiency in Python, Go, or advanced shell scripting alongside configuration management tools (Ansible/Salt) to interact with hardware APIs.

Nice-to-Haves

• Experience working within the OpenBMC ecosystem or building custom BMC firmware images.

• Deep operational familiarity with NVIDIA/Mellanox firmware management tools (mstflint, mlxup).

• Experience managing firmware lifecycles specifically within large-scale AI/ML training clusters or high-performance computing (HPC) environments.

Why Verda

• Cash + equity compensation along with various fringe benefits.

• Profitable operations with rapid, sustained growth.

• 31 nationalities, with 6 different ones on the management team.

• An opportunity to make a clear impact and work alongside world-class engineers, researchers, and partners across the global AI ecosystem.

Practicalities

• Work mode: Remote (EU)

title: Fincrime Compliance Manager
description:
Read this first

This role is not for most compliance people. It is narrow, exacting and unforgiving of vague work. If the "you will not enjoy this" section describes you, don't apply. We'd rather you didn't.

The job

You find risk, measure it and call it. You do not fix it. Every finding you write answers three things: what is broken, how bad it is, and what evidence proves it. You don't soften the rating and you don't propose the remedy. The business owns the fix. You own the truth about the risk.

What you will do

- Test our BSA/AML, KYC, OFAC and transaction monitoring controls end to end, independently of the teams that run them

- Rate every finding (high / medium / low) with evidence that holds up in front of a regulator

- Pull and analyze data yourself; you don't wait for someone to send you a report

- Challenge thresholds, alert logic and sampling assumptions with numbers, not opinions

- Track open issues until owners close them, and escalate when they don't

- Prepare us for regulator exams and audits, and be the person in the room who already knows the weak spots

What you need (non-negotiable)

- 4+ years in BSA/AML, FinCrime, internal audit or regulatory compliance

- Experience at a top-tier audit/advisory firm, in-house compliance, or both. Both is ideal.

- You have written findings that a regulator, auditor or board actually read

- You can say "this is high risk" to a senior leader and point to the regulation which proves it.

- Deep working knowledge of the BSA, USA PATRIOT Act, OFAC and FinCEN expectations

Nice to have

- Law degree (JD) or bar admission

- Degree in engineering, mathematics, statistics or another STEM field

- SQL: you can query transaction data yourself

- Python or R for analysis, sampling or testing alert logic

- Statistics: sampling design, hypothesis testing, threshold and model validation

CAMS, CRCM, CIA, CISA, CPA or CFE

- Exposure to AI or model risk (SR 11-7, NIST AI RMF)

You will not enjoy this role if

- You prefer building solutions to finding problems

- You need someone else to pull the data for you

- You round risk ratings down to keep people comfortable

title: Data Engineer (Fully Remote)
description:
The Role We Need

PadSplit is growing its analytics platform and needs a hands-on Data Engineer to work alongside our existing DE lead. This person will build and maintain ingestion and transformation pipelines across Dagster (or Airflow), dbt, and Snowflake, with supporting work in Python, Airbyte, and AWS. The role combines building new pipelines and data models with providing real coverage on critical paths - especially the daily Postgres → Snowflake → dbt flow and third-party API loads - all shipped through reviewed pull requests rather than one-off scripts.

The Person We Are Looking For

We're looking for a practitioner who thinks natively in dimensions, facts, and slowly changing dimensions - someone who knows when to use a full refresh versus an incremental load and how that choice affects idempotency and backfills. This person writes clear, reviewable PRs and gives equally thoughtful reviews, with attention to scoped diffs, sensible tests, and failure modes. They're comfortable in complex Python data flows and have enough AWS literacy to reason about task roles, buckets, and cross-account access without needing to own all of platform engineering.

Here's What You'll Be Doing Day-to-Day:

•
PR-driven shipping: Opening and merging pull requests for new or updated Dagster jobs, assets, schedules, and sensors, plus dbt models, tests, and documentation.

•
Infrastructure tweaks: Writing occasional Terraform for secrets, environment variables, or job sizing when a pipeline needs it.

•
Pipeline implementation: Building and debugging Python pipelines covering REST/API syncs, large Postgres extracts, Parquet loads, and Snowflake COPY operations.

•
Airbyte management: Configuring or troubleshooting Airbyte connections wherever managed sync is the right fit.

•
Production monitoring: Watching production runs and investigating failures related to IAM, OOM, Spot instances, or bad watermarks.

•
Backfills & catch-ups: Running backfills and incremental catch-ups with a clear story for what landed and why.

•
Modeling partnership: Working with analytics and product on dim/fct/x_fct design, incremental strategies, and data quality.

•
Code review & runbooks: Participating in code review, release prep, and writing short runbooks so others can operate your pipelines when you're out.

Here's What You'll Need to Be Successful:

•
Warehouse fundamentals: Solid grasp of relational databases and warehouse patterns - keys, grain, normalization vs. star schema, and how SCD behavior gets encoded.

•
Orchestration experience: Practical, hands-on Dagster (or Airflow) experience - not just writing SQL inside a scheduler UI.

•
dbt proficiency: Real experience building and maintaining models, tests, and documentation in dbt.

•
Python at scale: Comfort reading and writing Python that moves data at scale across extract, transform, and load steps.

•
AWS working knowledge: Practical familiarity with S3, IAM, and ECS/Fargate at a "debug my job" level.

•
EL tool familiarity: Experience with Airbyte or similar extract-and-load tools.

•
PR discipline: The discipline to write pull requests others can easily review, and to give equally rigorous reviews in return.

•
Reliability mindset: A track record of keeping pipelines healthy and modeling consistent across full refresh and incremental paths, without becoming a single point of failure.

- Manage Communications & Networks: Configure IP routing, subnets, and local network interfaces between flight controllers, companion computers, radios, and ground control stations.

- Hardware & Electronics Capability: Proven hands-on skills in wiring, custom cable assembly, bench soldering, and physical diagnostics using oscilloscopes and multimeters.

title: Senior Agentic Technical Writer
description:
Our Mission

At Redwood, we empower our customers with lights-out automation for their mission-critical business processes.

 

About Us

Redwood Software is the leading orchestration platform for the autonomous enterprise, driving business transformation at the lowest total cost of ownership. Redwood empowers organizations to intelligently automate and orchestrate mission-critical business and IT processes across complex ERP, hybrid cloud, data and emerging agentic AI systems. Through its SaaS-first automation fabric, with AI embedded across the automation lifecycle, Redwood accelerates the path to autonomous operations. Backed by 30 years of experience and trusted by more than 50% of the Fortune 50, Redwood helps organizations unlock human potential to focus on innovation, growth and what's next.

 

Core Values

• One Team. One Redwood

• Make Your Own Weather

• Obsess over Customer Success

• Work the Problem

• Be Curious

• Own the Outcome

• Respect Each Other

 

Your Impact

Redwood is rebuilding how documentation gets made. Content lives in Git as Markdown, ships through CI/CD, is reviewed by pull request next to product code, and is increasingly drafted by AI agents working from the product requirements, the code, and a structured content model. We are retiring our legacy authoring tool and moving every writer to this way of working.

You will be a senior writer who builds and runs that pipeline. You decide what an agent drafts and what a human must validate, you build the checks that catch failures, and you set the quality bar for AI-generated documentation. You also become a deep subject matter expert on Redwood's products and on the service orchestration and automation platform (SOAP) market they compete in, and you put what you learn back into the content model so every agent and writer inherits it.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You own a program, not a document set: the documentation pipeline and the content for a product area. You choose the approach on new work, guide more junior writers day to day, and have a significant say in documentation decisions for the business area. Not a people manager role.

Build and Run the Agentic Documentation Pipeline

• Design, build, and operate AI-assisted and agentic workflows that draft new content and update existing pages from product requirements, merged code, API specifications, Jira tickets, and release information.

• Define the handoffs: what the agent drafts, what the writer validates, how failures are detected, and how provenance is recorded. Publish the accuracy and review standards the team follows.

• Own the content model and context layer that agents read: structure, terminology, glossary, style rules, reusable components, and product knowledge, so output is consistent and machine-readable for customers, partners, and AI assistants.

• Build automated quality gates in CI: style and terminology linting, link checks, code sample and API reference validation, and an evaluation set that measures draft quality as models and prompts change.

• Detect drift: flag documentation that no longer matches the product after a code or API change.

• Measure the pipeline and report results: cycle time from release to published content, coverage, accuracy defects, reviewer edit effort, and cost per page.

• Keep an honest model of where agents fail on Redwood content, and move the human-AI boundary as models improve.

Docs as Code

• Own the Git workflow, Markdown/MDX authoring, build, and CI/CD publishing for your product area, with pull-request review alongside engineering.

• Lead migration of legacy content into structured, versioned Markdown, including information architecture, redirects, search, and versioning.

• Embed documentation in the delivery lifecycle: docs as a release gate, updates triggered by code and API changes, and documentation work that starts when the product definition is approved, in parallel with engineering rather

Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management.

You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. title: Account Manager, ACOs & Medicare Supplement (MediGap) Health Plans
description:
About Ceresti Health

Ceresti Health exists because dementia doesn’t just happen to a person - it happens to a family. We’ve built the first national, technology-enabled program that puts family caregivers at the center of dementia care, and we’re one of a small number of organizations selected by CMS to participate in the GUIDE Model. That’s not a credential. It’s a mandate. We’re building the infrastructure to transform how this country cares for people living with dementia - and the Account Manager position for ACOs & Med Supp plans is one of the most important roles in making that real.

Ceresti Health is a tech-enabled dementia care provider pioneering a differentiated model of care to activates family caregivers by giving them the knowledge, skills, and confident to detect an early change in their loved one’s condition. As one of the organizations selected by CMS to participatein the GUIDE Model and almost a decade of experience working in Medicare Advantage populations, we’re at the forefront of transforming dementia care nationwide.

Position Overview

The Account Manager, ACOs & MediGap is a high-ownership, relationship-intensive role at the intersection of performance management, physician awareness and education, carrier relationship development, and organizational change. You will serve as the primary partner for ACOs and Medicare Supplement carriers partnering with Ceresti - helping both ACOs and MediGap carriers strategically leverage the GUIDE Model to impact one of the costliest, most unmanaged cohorts in their populations. The Account Manager is responsible not just for account health, but for building the kind of trust that allows Ceresti to proactively enroll eligible beneficiaries on behalf of partner ACOs and MediGap plans.

This is not a reactive account management role. ACOs are complex organizations with physician stakeholders who are protective of their patient relationships, operational teams managing competing priorities, and leadership who need to see ROI in shared savings and operational relief. MediGapcarriers bring a different but equally complex dynamic - product and actuarial teams evaluating clinical value, compliance teams navigating CMS requirements, and member services teams that need seamless integration with GUIDE Model workflows. Your job is to earn and maintain trust across both channels - and to translate that trust into enrollment performance, program adoption, and measurable outcomes.

You’ll succeed here if you’re energized by complexity, comfortable navigating physician skepticism and carrier procurement cycles, and deeply motivated by what it means to get this right for families living with dementia.

Key Responsibilities

ACO & MediGap Carrier Relationship Management

• Serve as the primary account owner for assigned ACO and MediGap carrier partners from post-implementation through steady state.

• Build strong, trusted relationships with ACO leadership, operations teams, clinical leaders, and care management staff, as well as MediGap carrier product, compliance, and member services teams.

• Understand all components of the GUIDE Model and communicate GUIDE workflows to ACO care teams. For MediGap partners, understand how the GUIDE Model applies within the MediGap context and help carriers operationalize Ceresti's program for their member populations.

• Act as an internal liaison at Ceresti for each partner (ACO or MediGap carrier), ensuring the partner’s needs, constraints, and priorities are clearly understood, communicated, and appropriately addressed.

• Support contract adherence, shared savings alignment (ACOs), GUIDE Model performance targets (MediGap carriers), and ongoing partnership health.

Program Performance & Growth

• Own enrollment performance for assigned ACOs and MediGap carriers, including monitoring physician/care team referral flow (ACOs), member outreach and program utilization (MediGap), outreach effectiveness, and caregiver activation.
